quest.title: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III
quest.description: This is the final part of the journey to the Eternal Oasis. With any luck, this will prove a smooth trip...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Talk to Jeht and the others

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Next up is the third cave... Will the big iron ball still work?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: It is over 500 years old now. I doubt we can rely on it much longer, so we must act quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I shall lead the way. Our path gets smoother the further we proceed, it would seem.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Alright, come on, folks. Into the pilot cabin.

talks.objective: Drive the ancient machine to your destination
Check on the condition of the machine's interior

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Turning the panel on should do the job. Hmm, guess I'll let you do it.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Wouldn't be nice if I stole all the fun from you, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Azariq? Feeling unwell? We can take a break if you're tired.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: No, I'm good. Real good, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Jeht, we need to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm? Is it something important?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #...Before that, {NICKNAME}, I have a favor to ask of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Would you hand the Mother of the Jinn over into my keeping?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Well, well, aren't you a hasty lad? Far too hasty for your own good...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Azariq, you're like an elder brother to me, and I respect your guidance. But I... I don't understand. What's going on? Please, tell me!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: I'm doing this for the Tanit. We're getting close to our destination, and it is for the best that we take care of the Mother of the Jinn, rather than leave her in an outsider's hands.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is this... a request from Matriarch Babel?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: It is the rational choice. If she knew of this, she would give us her consent.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That wasn't my question. I'm asking you, is this a request from Matriarch Babel!?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: As I said, I do this for the Tanit. The Mother of the Jinn will be an invaluable asset in our hands, while in the hands of this outsider, she's nothing but a toy — a trinket.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Think about it! If we possess her power, we'll be able to recreate verdant oases in the desert again. Hasn't that been Matriarch Babel's pursuit this whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Once we finish this quest, Matriarch Babel will recognize your contributions by appointing you her successor, and your outlander friend will also be rewarded accordingly.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Everyone wins here. You, me... and of course, your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: You'd agree with me too, wouldn't you, outlander?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liloupar doesn't seem to like you much. Paimon doubts she'd come with you!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hehe, well said. But allow me to remind you: the contract between my Master and I can only be broken by death.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: You are right. My apologies.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: This is nonsense...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I said that this is nonsense, and you're full of it... traitor.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You insult me with your filthy lies, and I demand the right to respond with my blades.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Whoa... Just a second there, little wildcat. We were just having a friendly conversation. Why did you suddenly go berserk? Haven't we always been like family to each other?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Family? Perhaps... and perhaps not.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: First, you plot murder against our guests and taint our hospitality without Matriarch Babel's permission. This is an act of betrayal.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Second, you've learned technologies from the northerners, but you've refused to share the knowledge with the tribe. That is against our code.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: And third, you deceive your fellow tribes-people and place them in peril.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You're right, you know. I've always tried to view you as my brother. But what about you?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You have forgotten your mother's name. Thus, I demand that you cleanse your defilement with your weapons.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Wait. Calm down, calm down. Look, we're in the middle of the desert. If you kill me now, who will be able to prove your innocence?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: "Oh? So our little wildcat has finally bared her fangs against her tribe, huh?" That's what everyone will say. You'll be seen as a traitor.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Will someone who has betrayed their own tribe ever be accepted in the desert again?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: So what? The only reason I've let you live till now is that you never did us any harm. But now, that reason, too, is gone.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: I suggest you calm yourself down. We can still talk. There's no need to resort to violence.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I am calm! Pick up your blade!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: *sigh* I didn't expect things would go this far... I can only hope you will forgive me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, although, uh... she looks like a bottle right now, you should've asked for her consent first.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: *gasp* Wait, please, stop, little wildcat...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Shut up. You disgust me.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: *gasp* I'm not asking for your forgiveness. Just... hear me out...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Last words, huh? Make it quick.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: You... you let me down... Jeht, I thought you'd understand... *gasp* I reckoned we could work together...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: *gasp* You... struggled outside to make a living, too... We are so alike... You care about the Tanit... and you've always been loyal, no?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Please reconsider... *gasp* Think about it... Imagine what the Eternal Oasis will bring us... An infinite future, fertile fields, and endless opportunities...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Future children... will no longer have to beg for food from that city in the rainforest, nor will they need to learn the killer's trade. They will no longer have to rely on some strongman just to live with some dignity...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Think about it, Jeht... Babel is... no worthier... than us... to rule the Tanit...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: *gasp* Think, Jeht, think... You're a smart girl... You would... have done the same... for the Tanit...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Are you finished?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Go... If you... spare my life... I can get my friends on the outside to... spare yours, too...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Ha... Or what? Are you... *gasp* willing to be the first member of our tribe who... slaughters your own? I hope you have given thought to... the fate of traitors—

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "The one who fails to return alive is the traitor... or so you just told me."\nSays Jeht.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ahem. I understand if you may wish to mourn for your fellow tribesman or something... But I am obliged to tell you that this big thing will not hold up for much longer.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My master, for your own safety, we should leave as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yes... Let's go.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: No. I... want to throw up, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#You're awake! How are you feeling? Are you hurt? Can you still walk?}{F#You're awake. Phew... I thought... Sorry, I'm just being a little... Don't mind me. Um, are you hurt? Heh. Need me to carry you?}

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whoa... That was horrible... Are you alright, {NICKNAME}? Let's get out of here as soon as we can! Who knows if this big guy might explode again...

choices.text: I feel a little dizzy, but don't worry, I still recognize you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Still joking, huh? Alright, alright! Let's get out of here!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I am still here as well. My bottle remains intact.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Jeht, Paimon's more worried about you, honestly. You okay there?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Just got a few more scratches. Nothing much.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Alright, let us move on. A safe place, this is not.

choices.text: My rear hurts, but my legs still work...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I did a quick check on you. Your bones are fine. There's just a big bruise. Fortunately, you escaped serious injury.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But if you have trouble walking, let me help.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You shameless traitor! You dare to show up here? Explain yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Wait, please, calm down...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I am calm! You just mentioned Azariq, didn't you? I've already dealt with that filthy creature, and I wouldn't mind having a repeat performance with you!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: I thought you saw him as your brother...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Brother, my foot! And you, traitor, had better take stock of your situation. Each word you say could be your last!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: I... He... Wait, I'm really confused right now. Just give me a second to organize my thoughts, please!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Organize your thoughts? Of what? Of teaming up with the Fatui? And you guys! You're with him, aren't you!?

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Skirmisher
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Skirmisher
dialogues.text: Uh... It's a long story, if you would...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Shut it! I'm so sick and tired of having to "be reasonable" with the bad guys. I don't care what you have to say. My blades, though, have lots of things to say to you!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Wait...!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmph... I need to wipe my blades. Help me keep watch.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Judge the criminal first, then find the evidence, huh... Whatever. It makes no difference.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Azariq... So he wanted to murder Matriarch Babel, then become the co-leader of the Tanit with me by "marriage"... and then make us all puppets for the northerners?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...And that's why he had to take you, who might already know what was going on, out of the picture, and gain control over the Jinni. From the very beginning, he had assumed that I would trust him absolutely and go along with his scheme...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I trusted him so much, too! I never... I never imagined he was such a disgusting person.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Alright. Revenge has been had, and the drama comes to a close. Drumroll please! And who has had the last laugh? Oh my, it's our little Jeht!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *sigh* This is exhausting. Shall we proceed?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Matriarch Babel needs to know about this.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Returning now just to give her a report? Oh, I wouldn't call that wisdom.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Do you really think that desert woman would believe that these two stupid men — and not you — are the traitors if you return empty-handed?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: For the sake of argument, let's assume you have proof of their betrayal. But knowing what you do of the desert dwellers' traditions, do you think your tribe will focus on the evidence and not pay a single slice of attention to the fact that you killed your tribesmen?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Will Matriarch Babel have eyes only for the proof and forgive the shame caused by your brutal slaughter? I, for one, think she'd much rather hear some good news.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: If you wish to return to rest for a moment, you can. But speak nothing of what transpired here. That is my advice.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Agreed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... You two didn't argue at all. That sure is a new one.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If we didn't have more important things to do, I would've cut their heads off and taken them back with me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well then, let's move on.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright. I will watch your back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, where are we going?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The big iron ball is totally broken, and there are no clear paths around.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Worry not, little one, you still have me.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Well, there is this hole over there that the big iron ball created as it fell. We should be able to reach our destination if we go through it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So you can sense stuff like that too? Wow, you're better than a compass! Maybe Paimon should call you Liloupass from now on.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: As I said, my fragment guides me. Let us go. Enter that big iron ball, and we should find a path from there.

choices.text: Why do villains always leave a trail to be found...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Beats Paimon... Hey, that's not the point!

talks.objective: Follow Liloupar's instructions and return to the machine's interior
Follow Liloupar's instructions and return to the machine's interior
Enter the tunnel alongside the inside of the machine

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: How utterly stupid. The tiger pulled out her fangs and smoothed her teeth just to welcome a bride.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Now that the tiger is just one step away from her goal, she just gives up everything else — The tail? Useless! The ears? What are they for!?

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: But remember, "If not handled well, your scimitar's blade could be turned against yourself." Hmph, I'm not talking about you, golden canary. I speak of...

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: You'd better watch out for your friend Jeht. Take care of her, hide her fangs, and smooth her raised hackles.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So... are we just one last step away from reaching the Eternal Oasis now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the matter? Are you unhappy, Jeht?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hmm... I don't know. I mean, I do look forward to fulfilling my parents' dreams at last.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But I can't help but get mixed feelings when I think of all that we've been through along the way.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Although I now have the tribe to call home, betrayals and schemes are never far from me. Are the Tanit truly where I belong? Have I really been accepted by them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... Let's not wallow in the sad things, Jeht. The past is the past... and anyway, we've beaten all the bad guys now, haven't we?

choices.text: Paimon's right. It's water under the bridge now.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah, you're right. Let them sink into the sands. We have more important things to do!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But... *sigh* When Dad was with me, I could say "Home is where Dad is." But now, I'm all alone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah, stop wallowing in self-pity, Jeht. You're better than this! Also, we're here for you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: *chuckle* Don't get mad, Paimon. But you're right. I need to keep my chin up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now we're talking! Huh. Aren't we supposed to head out now? We can go up using this platform, right?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, alright! Now, enough sentimentality. Let's go!

choices.text: It's not the end of the world even if that isn't where you truly belong.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ha, you're so carefree! You know, I was starting to forget that you're a traveler, unconstrained anywhere by anything or anyone!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It's only that... hehe... when Dad was with me, I could say "Home is where Dad is." But now, I'm all by myself.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, I'm alright. I'm in a good mood, actually. It's just... *sigh*

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Dad went through all kinds of setbacks and betrayals in his adventures, and I just realized that I'm on the same unfortunate path as him.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Although I now have the tribe to call home, betrayals and schemes are never far from me. Are the Tanit truly where I belong? Have I really been accepted by them?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: #What's the matter, {NICKNAME}? Did you encounter any trouble during your adventure?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: If you are thinking about Aderfi, he will soon reap what he has sown. Or did someone else offend you?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I will handle them properly.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you see flaring flames and blunt blades...\nYou see the freezing moonlight and viscous honey...\nThrough the golden honey, you see the underlying scheme...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The princess sees the consequences of her innocuous error, her sanity giving way to madness...\nHer invincible husband is shaken by the tragedy, his greedy heart blinded by ecstasy...\nAll the sorrow, joy, and madness are finally turned into food for the Jinn-Mother to devour...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "It is curtains for the carnivorous Night of Honey — Such is the end of the Jinni's lover..."

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#Listen here, Jinni. If anything happens to him, I'll get you for that.}{F#Listen here, Jinni. If this does any harm to her, I'll get you for that.}

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Harm? Oh, come now. Addiction, though... Now that is a more probable risk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Addiction is not okay, either! It's unacceptable no matter what!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The golden honey, the golden scheme... Departure breaks the heart, yet the kingdom lives on under the usurper's rule...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You have seen that which I speak of.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I once believed that he would bring this land into a bright future, but he proved no different from the other shallow, mortal tyrants. I was furious... No, I was in pain.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I was once deeply and madly in love with him, but when I was betrayed like that... Only destruction three times greater than that love could quell my sorrow and pain... Perhaps.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: In short... I used the hands and hearts of my own children to complete an impeccable killing. Such is the consequence of betrayal.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Let's get moving. This is giving me goosebumps.

choices.text: You... It was you who murdered them...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It was not "murder"... It was punishment. For my lover, and for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Right there in the center is the Crystal Goblet of Al-Ahmar. If we get there, we should be able to find a way to enter the Eternal Oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What is it? Got anything to say, Jinni?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Something smells familiar here. But no, it's nothing important.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Anyway, let us head over there first. Please be careful, my master. I will protect you from the sandstorm.

talks.objective: Go to the Crystal Goblet of Al-Ahmar

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: C—Careful! I sense a strange power!
...You. The destroyer of Gurabad, the Mother of the Despicable.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I have returned, sister.
"Sister"? I don't understand. Are you calling me... "sister"?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Yes. Ferigees, my sister... I have returned.

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: #You are here to see our mistress, aren't you? Let me guess, you have brought your new master and... {M#his}{F#her} desert slave?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This person's starting to tick me off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, sure sounds like she's Liloupar's sister, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems to run in the family...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... If that's the case, Paimon certainly doesn't want to be a guest at their place...

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: Hmph. You cannot pass.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Ferigees, I understand your concerns. I would even be willing to bow in apology, but please, let me see our slumbering mistress, if for but a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: You are worthy no longer, fallen traitor. There is no place for you now in the oasis realm.

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: Leave now, before my patience runs dry and these mechanical shackles rumble, and never show yourselves here again.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Sister, you shed the form of a Jinni and constrained yourself to this husk for thousands of years. Is this the "survival" that you so desired to pursue?

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: So, you dispense your kindness to me? Despicable traitor, my shackles have nothing to do with you!

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: Ugh... Agh... Ahh...! The shackles... they tighten... Leave! Leave now!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My master, if I may so ask, please assist me in freeing my sister from her suffering...

choices.text: Hold on, I don't get it...

response.speaker: Ferigees
response.text: Still so arrogant and inconstant... You disappoint me, my sister.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah! Paimon hasn't even figured out what's going on yet, and we're about to fight already!?

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: You broke this shell... My spirit and form... shall soon vanish with it also...

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: Folly... Just like some mere mortal... Why... What kind of desire... Did you hold...

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: The empty tomb... It will crumble... Just like me... and just like you, who are not whole...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I know, my sister. Still, I must go there, where our mistress slumbers. That is where the answers I seek lie.

dialogues.speaker: Ferigees
dialogues.text: No... Nothing there... But... the coalescence of... regret...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Farewell, my sister.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The ancient mechanism named "Ferigees," or perhaps the Jinni "Ferigees" who indwelled the mechanism, is silenced forever.

talks.objective: Go to the center of the platform

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, alas for this big iron ball... It is in pieces now.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: This looks like someone tossed a little wildcat into a sack and threw the sack into the porcelain store...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *chuckle* That would be quite the scene!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hey! I heard that! I know what you're talking about!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: These people are...? You... you despicable traitors!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: These people... Why are they here?

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Come on, Azariq, we've been waiting for ages... Wait, why are you here!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Seems like Aderfi dropped something. Let's check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hehe, you've gotten familiar with desert robberies, haven't you, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't you make it sound like it's something normal!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Aha, all set. It guides us once more. Now, let us simply follow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the last mechanism. Shall we go check out the "Goblet" at the center?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Under Liloupar's protection, you pass the leaguer of the sandstorm and land safely on the platform.
